Kai (People Ops): Quick one — Isabel's spouse just got a green card and moved off Medicaid in the US on 2026-06-10. Can we add them midyear? What proof do we need for eligibility and any immigration docs?
Isabel L: They were on Medicaid until 6/10, now permanent resident. We live together since 2025-11-01. I have the green card scan, a Medicaid termination letter, and joint lease. Is that enough?
Tariq - Benefits: Congrats! That's usually a QLE (loss of other coverage + change in household). Docs we need: (1) proof of loss of prior coverage (Medicaid termination or letter), (2) proof of current immigration status (copy of green card or USCIS I-551), (3) proof of residence/financial interdependence (joint lease, shared bank statement), and (4) dependent SSN for enrollment.
Isabel L: We don't have the SSN yet  spouse applied and has an ITIN pending. Can we enroll with ITIN and update later?
Tariq - Benefits: We need a valid tax identifier for benefits enrollment. If they only have ITIN pending, we can provisionally add them for plan selection but final enrollment and ID cards require SSN or ITIN on file. If ITIN arrives within 30 days we can finalize without delay.
ImmigrationBot: Note: green card holders may have travel/processing delays. For HR, do not store full alien registration numbers in non-secure channels.
Kai (People Ops): Timeline Q: Is the 30-day QLE window from 6/10? Can effective date be 6/1 or 6/10?
Tariq - Benefits: QLE window is 30 days from the event (6/10). Effective date can be retro to 6/1 only if docs clearly show loss of coverage on or before 6/1; otherwise effective date is the date of the event (6/10) or 7/1 depending on carrier rules. We often request Medicaid termination showing last day of coverage. Carriers have different backdate rules.
Isabel L: The Medicaid letter says coverage ended 6/09. Lease shows move-in 2025-11-01. I'll upload both. Any privacy rules for the green card copy?
Tariq - Benefits: Redact any full alien registration numbers and SSN before upload; we only need last 4 for verification. Use the secure HR portal: https://hr.redwood.com/upload (choose "QLE - Immigration/coverage loss"). Do not attach to slack or email.
Juno (Payroll): Heads up on payroll: if benefits effective date is set to 6/10 or 6/1 with retro, payroll will compute retro premiums and either lump-sum or spread across next N pay periods (employee choice). If ITIN/SSN arrives late we may delay final deductions until confirmed.
Isabel L: Uploading now via portal. Should I include a screenshot of Medicaid site or only the official letter?
Tariq - Benefits: Official termination letter preferred. Screenshots accepted if timestamped and accompanied by official doc. Also include proof of identity (passport) redacted.
Kai (People Ops): I'll calendar a 25-day follow-up to ensure submission within 30-day window. @Tariq please confirm carrier acceptance once you review.
Tariq - Benefits: Received uploads this AM. Reviewing with carrier. If approved, we'll confirm effective date and notify payroll. If carrier needs SSN/ITIN, we'll flag Isabel to update when available. :thumbsup:
